title: Impact of Social Support on the Standard of Living and Psychological Well-Being of Women Exposed to Violent Conflicts
text_snippet: Impact of Social Support on the Standard of Living and Psychological Well-Being of Women Exposed to Violent Conflicts Women in Plateau State, Nigeria, have experienced prolonged exposure to conflict caused by the Boko Haram insurgency, Fulani herder attacks, and ethno-religious violence, resulting in displacement, trauma, and economic vulnerability. Although humanitarian assistance has been provided, evidence-based psychosocial interventions remain limited. This quasi-experimental study evaluated the effectiveness of social support interventions on psychological well-being and standard of living among conflict-affected women in Plateau State Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) camps. A pretest-posttest control group design was employed with 80 women (aged 18-60 years) randomly assigned to two groups: social support intervention (n=40) and control (n=40). The intervention was delivered over 12 weeks. Psychological well-being was measured using the Ryff Psychological Well-Being Scale, and standard of living was assessed using a validated Standard of Living Index. Data were analyzed using ANCOVA and independent t-tests. The social support intervention produced significant improvements compared to controls. title: Tolerance, Ngajeni and Nrimo as Javanese Value to Reduce Bullying Behavior
text_snippet: Tolerance, Ngajeni and Nrimo as Javanese Value to Reduce Bullying Behavior Bullying remains a serious problem that can hinder the development of students' potential and trigger long-term psychological impacts, such as social disintegration, negative self-evaluation, and depression. This study seeks to examine the impact of Javanese behavior on bullying conduct among students. The study used a quantitative approach with a survey design involving 943 Javanese high school and vocational high school students (429 males; 514 females). Data were collected through a Google Form-based Javanese behavior and bullying behavior questionnaire. title: Indonesian Cultural Empathy Scale (ICES): Development and Validation of a Contextualized Measure
text_snippet: Indonesian Cultural Empathy Scale (ICES): Development and Validation of a Contextualized Measure Multicultural societies require culturally grounded instruments to assess empathy in ways that reflect local religious, communal, and national value systems. However, widely used empathy scales are predominantly developed within Western frameworks and may not adequately capture culturally embedded expressions of empathy in Indonesia. This study aims to develop and validate the Indonesian Cultural Empathy Scale (ICES) by constructing contextually grounded indicators and examining its factorial structure and construct validity. An exploratory sequential mixed-methods design was employed, beginning with qualitative inquiry through interviews, observation, and documentation to identify core domains of cultural empathy. These domains were integrated with ethnocultural empathy theory and the 18 National Character Pillars to construct scale indicators and items, which were subsequently evaluated through expert judgment. The quantitative phase involved large-scale survey administration and factor-based validation analysis. title: Gender Differences in Self Acceptance among Economically Disadvantaged Senior High School Students in Bukittinggi, West Sumatera, Indonesia
text_snippet: Gender Differences in Self Acceptance among Economically Disadvantaged Senior High School Students in Bukittinggi, West Sumatera, Indonesia Self-acceptance issues can affect students’ developmental tasks and their ability to adapt within educational environments. This study aimed to analyze the level of students’ self-acceptance and to examine differences in self-acceptance between male and female students from underprivileged backgrounds. The study employed a quantitative approach with a comparative research design. The participants involved high school students from underprivileged families selected through a total sampling technique. Data were collected through the administration of a Self-Acceptance Scale developed based on a Likert-scale model in accordance with indicators of self-acceptance. Data analysis was conducted descriptively by considering measures of central tendency and data distribution, while difference analysis was performed using the independent sample t-test. The findings revealed that students’ self-acceptance was generally categorized as high for both male and female students. The results also indicated that there was no significant difference in self-acceptance based on gender, suggesting that gender was not a major factor influencing the self-acceptance of students from underprivileged backgrou

title: Marriage Readiness among Final-Year University Students: The Role of Emotional Maturity and Interpersonal Communication Skills as Predictive Factors
text_snippet: Marriage Readiness among Final-Year University Students: The Role of Emotional Maturity and Interpersonal Communication Skills as Predictive Factors Marriage readiness is an essential developmental task in early adulthood, yet many final-year students face the transition to marriage without adequate psychological and interpersonal preparedness. Empirical research that comprehensively identifies personal competencies as predictors of marriage readiness in this transitional phase remains limited. This study aims to analyze and examine the predictive role of emotional maturity and interpersonal communication skills on marriage readiness among final-year students. A correlational quantitative design was employed with unmarried final-year students selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using an emotional maturity scale based on emotional regulation and stability, the Interpersonal Communication Competence Scale (ICCS), and a marriage readiness scale covering psychological, emotional, social, and marital value dimensions. Multiple regression analysis was conducted after testing statistical assumptions, validity, and reliability. title: The Role of Shyness in the Adaptability of First-Year Students with Peer Attachment as a Moderator
text_snippet: The Role of Shyness in the Adaptability of First-Year Students with Peer Attachment as a Moderator Many first-year students still experience difficulties adjusting to the academic, social, and emotional environment of college. Furthermore, personality factors such as shyness are thought to influence the success rate of new students' adjustment to the demands of campus life. This study aims to analyze the effect of shyness on first-year students’ self-adjustment ability as well as the moderating role of peer attachment. The research employed a cross-sectional design with a population of 100 freshmen in Surabaya. Data were collected through questionnaires consisting of shyness, peer attachment, and self-adjustment scales. Moderated regression analysis was used to examine the relationships among the variables. The results showed that shyness had a significant negative effect on freshmen’s self-adjustment ability (p 0.05). These findings indicate that students who experience shyness tend to face difficulties in adapting, whereas peer support alone is insufficient to reduce the negative impact of shyness. This study concludes that shyness greatly affects new student acclimation. Students with high shyness may struggle with academics, socializing, mood regulation, and campus activitie

title: The Dynamics of Students’ Independence and Basic Psychological Needs: A Comparative Study of General Boarding Schools and Islamic Boarding Schools
text_snippet: The Dynamics of Students’ Independence and Basic Psychological Needs: A Comparative Study of General Boarding Schools and Islamic Boarding Schools The achievement of independence is a crucial developmental task during adolescence; however, boarding school environments often create a dilemma between collective disciplinary control and students’ need for individual autonomy. Imbalances in the fulfillment of basic psychological needs at school may lead to low initiative, maladaptive behavior, and disciplinary violations due to weak self-regulation. This study aimed to analyze differences in the level of independence and fulfillment of basic psychological needs between students in general boarding schools and Islamic boarding schools. The study employed a comparative descriptive quantitative approach involving 175 students as research participants, consisting of 90 students from general boarding schools and 85 students from Islamic boarding schools. Data were collected using the Adolescent Independence Scale and the validated Basic Psychological Needs Scale. Data analysis was conducted using the Independent Sample t-test. title: The Effectiveness of Cognitive Behavioral Group Counseling in Reducing Fear of Missing Out (FOMO) Among Vocational High School Students
text_snippet: The Effectiveness of Cognitive Behavioral Group Counseling in Reducing Fear of Missing Out (FOMO) Among Vocational High School Students Excessive dependence on social media among adolescents often triggers social anxiety, namely the phenomenon of Fear of Missing Out (FOMO). This condition creates emotional pressure due to the fear of missing out on information or digital trends, which ultimately disrupts students' concentration and psychological well-being. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of group counseling interventions using a cognitive behavioral approach in reducing FOMO levels among vocational school students. The research subjects involved a population of 70 students, with a core sample of 20 students divided into experimental and control groups. Additionally, this study involved 31 tenth-grade MP students as test subjects for the instrument to ensure the accuracy of the measurement tool. Data collection used a Likert-scale FOMO questionnaire that had undergone validity and reliability testing with a Cronbach's Alpha value of 0.927. The data analysis technique used was the Independent Samples T-Test parametric statistical test with the assistance of the SPSS program. title: Building Psychological Resilience in Cancer Patients: A Systematic Review of Internal–External Factors and Intervention Effectiveness
text_snippet: Building Psychological Resilience in Cancer Patients: A Systematic Review of Internal–External Factors and Intervention Effectiveness Psychological resilience is the ability to adapt and recover from cancer-related stress. However, studies on its factors and psychosocial interventions remain conceptually and empirically inconsistent. This study aimed to analyze the conceptual framework of resilience, explore the internal and external factors influencing resilience in adult cancer patients, and evaluate the effectiveness of resilience-based psychosocial interventions. This study employed a systematic review method based on the PRISMA guidelines. The subjects of the study consisted of scientific articles discussing resilience among adult cancer patients. Data were collected through literature searches in reputable scientific databases and analyzed using narrative synthesis through systematic processes of study selection, data extraction, and quality appraisal. The findings revealed that resilience is influenced by internal factors, including hope, optimism, self-efficacy, emotional regulation, spirituality, and adaptive coping strategies, as well as external factors such as social support, clinical conditions, and psychosocial services. title: The Effectiveness of Group Counseling Using Cognitive Restructuring Techniques in Addressing Low Self-Confidence Among Bullying Victims
text_snippet: The Effectiveness of Group Counseling Using Cognitive Restructuring Techniques in Addressing Low Self-Confidence Among Bullying Victims Bullying is a form of aggressive behavior that harms others and can have detrimental consequences for its victims. One of the adverse effects of bullying is low self-confidence among students who experience it. This study aimed to examine the effectiveness of group counseling using cognitive restructuring techniques in improving the self-confidence of students who are victims of bullying. A quantitative approach was employed using a quasi-experimental design with a nonequivalent control group. The population consisted of 44 students from two different classes. From this population, 24 students identified as having low self-confidence were selected as the research sample. Pretests and posttests were administered to determine differences between the experimental and control groups. Data were collected using a Likert-scale self-confidence instrument, in which higher scores indicated lower levels of self-confidence. Data were analyzed using an Independent Samples t-test in JASP software. The results revealed a difference in posttest scores between the experimental and control groups. title: Coping With Single Parenthood in Southwest Nigeria: Psychosocial Challenges and Adaptive Strategies Among Parents in Oye-Ekiti
text_snippet: Coping With Single Parenthood in Southwest Nigeria: Psychosocial Challenges and Adaptive Strategies Among Parents in Oye-Ekiti Single parents are increasingly common in developing societies and often face economic, psychosocial, social, and support-related challenges. Therefore, deeper understanding is needed of how they adapt to these conditions. This study aimed to analyze the psychosocial challenges experienced by single parents and examine the adaptive coping strategies they employ in navigating the demands of single parenthood. The study employed a quantitative survey research design involving 100 single parents selected as research participants. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire that measured psychosocial challenges, including stress, anxiety, and depression, as well as coping strategies related to economic engagement, personal character development, social image management, and family support. The collected data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistical techniques. The findings indicate that extended family support is the most dominant coping strategy, followed by efforts to build more positive social perceptions of single parents, engagement in productive economic activities, and strengthening personal resilience and moral values. title: A Cognitive-Behavioral Counseling Model Using Self-Management Techniques to Enhance Career Maturity
text_snippet: A Cognitive-Behavioral Counseling Model Using Self-Management Techniques to Enhance Career Maturity Low career maturity among students remains a serious problem characterized by a lack of understanding of self-potential, career goals, and weak ability to make career decisions independently. This study aims to analyze the tendency of students' career choice profiles and the effectiveness of the cognitive behavioral counseling model with self-management techniques in improving the career maturity of grade XI students. This study used a quasi-experimental design with a nonequivalent pretest-posttest control group design. The research subjects consisted of 64 students divided into an experimental group and a control group. The research instrument was a career maturity questionnaire that had been tested for validity and reliability. The results showed that the level of career maturity of students before being given treatment was in the moderate category, which indicated that most students still experienced confusion in determining career direction and future planning. title: Technostress and Academic Resilience Among First-Year College Students: A Cross-Sectional Study
text_snippet: Technostress and Academic Resilience Among First-Year College Students: A Cross-Sectional Study When entering education at the university level, first-year students are usually required to master technology—the use of technology as the main support in learning and facilitating all student academic activities. Over time, this can lead to technology-based stress which then leads to poor academic resilience abilities formed by first-year students. This study aims to prove the relationship between technostress and academic resilience in first-year students. This study used a quantitative method with a cross-sectional bivariate correlational design. A total of 423 first-year students became research participants using the accidental sampling technique. Research measurements used Technostress Creators (α = 0.981) and Academic Resilience Scale-30 (α = 0.982). title: Cognitive Behavioral Counseling Using Systematic Desensitization Techniques to Reduce Anxiety in High School Students
text_snippet: Cognitive Behavioral Counseling Using Systematic Desensitization Techniques to Reduce Anxiety in High School Students This research is motivated by the high level of learning anxiety experienced by high school students, which has a negative impact on the learning process and outcomes. Learning anxiety arises due to irrational thinking patterns, academic pressure, and students' inability to manage emotional responses adaptively. This study aims to describe the effectiveness of cognitive behavioral counseling with systematic desensitization techniques in minimizing students' learning anxiety in high school. title: Bullying Behaviour among Middle School Students in Rural and Town Communities
text_snippet: Bullying Behaviour among Middle School Students in Rural and Town Communities The gap in access to information and the quality of education between urban and rural institutions motivated this study. This research on bullying aligns with the Indonesian government's commitment to address three key issues in education: bullying, intolerance, and sexual violence. This study aims to investigate factors influencing bullying behaviour among junior high school students directed at their peers in rural and urban communities. The study employed quantitative methods, with 715 students participating. Junior high school students were selected as the study sample due to the higher incidence of violence compared to senior high school students. Data collection was conducted using the Qualtrics system. The study findings indicate that student residence influences bullying behaviour, with students in rural communities engaging in less bullying than those in urban areas. Gender and grade level variables also significantly influence bullying behaviour among junior high school students in rural and urban communities across Indonesia. title: Relaxation Assisted by Gending Sriwijaya Music as an Effort to Reduce Social Anxiety in Students
text_snippet: Relaxation Assisted by Gending Sriwijaya Music as an Effort to Reduce Social Anxiety in Students Social anxiety among adolescents is a psychological problem that can hinder social interaction skills, reduce participation in academic activities, and negatively affect emotional development and psychological well-being. Increasing social demands, educational pressures, and the limited availability of culturally relevant intervention strategies have made social anxiety an important issue that requires effective and contextualized treatment approaches. This study aimed to analyze, evaluate, and examine the effectiveness of a relaxation technique assisted by Gending Sriwijaya traditional music in reducing social anxiety among adolescents. The study employed a quantitative approach using a pretest-posttest control group experimental design. The participants consisted of 14 students identified as having high levels of social anxiety and were assigned to experimental and control groups. Data were collected using an adapted version of the Social Anxiety Scale for Adolescents (SAS-A), which had undergone a validation process and was used to measure participants’ social anxiety levels before and after the intervention. title: The Effectiveness of the Solution Focused Brief Group Counseling Guidebook in Reducing Fear of Missing Out (FOMO) in Students
text_snippet: The Effectiveness of the Solution Focused Brief Group Counseling Guidebook in Reducing Fear of Missing Out (FOMO) in Students This study aims to develop a Solution Focused Brief group counseling guidebook that meets the criteria of acceptability, which consists of four aspects, namely: accuracy, usefulness, feasibility, and appropriateness, and to test its effectiveness in reducing FOMO in adolescents. The study uses the Borg and Gall research and development (R&D) model, which consists of seven stages. Research participants included expert validators, guidance counselors, and students. Data were collected through questionnaires using validity assessment instruments administered to experts and prospective users to assess the level of acceptability of the developed guidebook, as well as questionnaires using FOMO instruments administered to students. Data analysis was conducted by applying product validity methods and effectiveness tests through a comparison of pretest and posttest results. The effectiveness test results showed that the intervention using the FOMORE guide had a significant impact on reducing FOMO in adolescents. title: Development of an Inclusive Campus Model Based in Universal Design for Learning in Supporting the Achievement of Students with Disabilities
text_snippet: Development of an Inclusive Campus Model Based in Universal Design for Learning in Supporting the Achievement of Students with Disabilities Higher education in Indonesia still faces challenges in building inclusive campuses for students with disabilities, particularly in physical-digital access, lecturer awareness, and support infrastructure. Therefore, an adaptive, inclusive, and equitable campus model is needed. This study aims to develop an inclusive campus model based on Universal Design for Learning (UDL) to improve the academic achievement of students with disabilities. The research method used is development research with the ADDIE (Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation) model. The research subjects consisted of 240 participants, including students with disabilities, managers of Disability Services Units, and the general public from various universities. Data were collected through literature studies, in-depth interviews, observations, and questionnaires, then analyzed using a qualitative descriptive approach and expert validation. The results of the study show that the implementation of the UDL-based inclusive campus model can improve academic accessibility, learning flexibility, and social support for students with disabilities. title: Development and Validation of the Indonesian Version Self-Harm Inventory Using Rasch Model
text_snippet: Development and Validation of the Indonesian Version Self-Harm Inventory Using Rasch Model Self-harm among adolescents is currently a hot topic in various countries. This phenomenon has become a concern for counsellors and society in general. This study aims to develop an Indonesian version of the Self-Harm Inventory that can detect self-harm behaviour among high school students. The method used in this study is the ADDIE model, and the analysis was conducted using Rasch analysis. The pilot sample comprised 50 high school students, and the sample for estimating the prevalence of self-harm comprised 256 students selected by simple random sampling. The scale was developed in accordance with Indonesian culture. The results showed that the SHI scale had excellent validity and reliability based on item fit parameters, person-item reliability, and no item DIF was found in the inventory. The study also revealed the prevalence of self-harm among high school students identified using the SHI and showed that student self-harm behaviour was in the very low category. These findings are expected to form the basis for appropriate prevention and eradication interventions to build positive mental health and achieve psychological well-being among students.

In addition, indigenous knowledge is usually treated as a supplementary story rather than an operational introduction to analyze and elaborate practical family counseling programs. The purpose of this study is to understand the pupose, value construction and practical function of Beseprah as local wisdom and expand its implementation for a cultially relevant family counseling model. title: Forgiveness and Subjective Well-being in Students Who are Victims of Toxic Relationships
text_snippet: Forgiveness and Subjective Well-being in Students Who are Victims of Toxic Relationships University students who experience toxic relationships frequently encounter challenges in achieving subjective well-being due to the psychological consequences of unhealthy relational dynamics. These difficulties may stem from an impaired capacity to forgive and to reconcile with the situation. This study aims to examine the association between forgiveness and subjective well-being among students who have been victims of toxic relationships. The research employed a quantitative approach using a bivariate correlational design. A total of 139 students who met the criteria for having experienced a toxic relationship participated in the study through purposive sampling. Forgiveness was assessed using the TRIM-18, whereas subjective well-being was measured using the Satisfaction With Life Scale (SWLS) and the Positive and Negative Affect Schedule (PANAS). Pearson’s correlation analysis revealed no significant association between forgiveness and subjective well-being (r = 0.048, p > 0.05). Specifically, forgiveness was not significantly correlated with life satisfaction, positive affect, or negative affect. title: School Counselors’ Meaning in Life as a Foundation for Professional Well-being and Professionalism: A Phenomenological Study
text_snippet: School Counselors’ Meaning in Life as a Foundation for Professional Well-being and Professionalism: A Phenomenological Study The complex and demanding role of school counselors requires a strong sense of meaning in life (MIL). MIL plays a vital role in helping counselors manage stress, maintain psychological well-being, and strengthen their professional identity. Burnout and loss of purpose as counselors are complex issues in the professionalism of counselors. The purpose of this study is to explore the subjective, lived experiences of school counselors in finding and constructing MIL through their professional roles. The research employed a qualitative phenomenological approach. Data were collected through in-depth interviews and observations with five school counselors. Data analysis was conducted through three stages: reduction, reflection, and refinement. The findings reveal four key themes in the meaning in life of school counselors: (1) a sense of peace and fulfilment in performing their professional roles, (2) growing together with students, (3) the presence of support systems that sustain their career journey, and (4) spirituality that strengthens their professional commitment. title: Psychological Distress, Neuroticism, and Loneliness in Adolescents from Broken Homes
text_snippet: Psychological Distress, Neuroticism, and Loneliness in Adolescents from Broken Homes The mental health landscape among Indonesian adolescents is showing an increasingly alarming trend. Data indicate that approximately 15.5 million adolescents, or 34.9% of that age group, are struggling with at least one form of mental health issue. Among the various problems faced, loneliness holds a crucial position as it not only affects emotional well-being but also significantly influences the social development of adolescents. This study was conducted to examine the role of psychological distress and neuroticism as predictor variables of loneliness among broken home adolescents in Indonesia. The research sample consisted of 485 adolescents aged 15-21 years from various regions across Indonesia, selected through purposive sampling. The study employed a quantitative approach using multiple linear regression analysis. The instruments used were the Kessler Psychological Distress Scale (K-10), the NEO Five Factor Inventory (NEO-FFI), and the De Jong-Gierveld Loneliness Scale (DJGLS). The findings showed that both the major and minor hypotheses were accepted. title: Healthy Lifestyle Behavior, Hardiness, and Psychological Distress in the Sandwich Generation
text_snippet: Healthy Lifestyle Behavior, Hardiness, and Psychological Distress in the Sandwich Generation Approximately 56 million productive-age individuals in Indonesia are classified as the Sandwich Generation, facing psychological pressure due to their dual roles in caring for aging parents while raising children. This pressure may increase psychological distress, highlighting the need to understand protective factors that can mitigate its impact. This study aims to analyze the roles of healthy lifestyle and hardiness as predictors of psychological distress among Indonesia’s Sandwich Generation. The sample consisted of 432 respondents obtained through accidental sampling over a one-month period. A quantitative approach with multiple linear regression analysis was employed. The instruments used were the Health-Promoting Lifestyle Profile II (HPLP-II), Hardiness Scale, and Depression Anxiety Stress Scale (DASS-21). The results revealed that, simultaneously, healthy lifestyle and hardiness significantly predicted psychological distress. However, only hardiness emerged as a significant individual predictor. title: Counseling Guideline of Spiritual Cognitive Behavior Technique to Optimize Students’ Personality Potential
text_snippet: Counseling Guideline of Spiritual Cognitive Behavior Technique to Optimize Students’ Personality Potential Personality problems among university students, such as identity crises, low self-confidence, and difficulties in self-regulation, indicate that their personality potential has not been fully optimized. This study aims to develop a counseling guideline, the Spiritual Cognitive Behavior Technique to Optimize Students’ Personality Potential (SCBTec-SPP), as an innovation in counseling services. The research employed a research and development approach using the Borg and Gall model, limited to the first five stages: research and information collecting, planning, developing a preliminary form of product, preliminary field testing, and main product revision. The research subjects consisted of 100 students for the preliminary study, 3 experts (media, content, and counseling practitioners), and 35 students for the practicality test. The research instruments included the Student Personality Potential Questionnaire, expert validation sheets, and a practicality questionnaire. Data were analyzed using percentage techniques and the Content Validity Index (CVI). title: Research Trends of Suicidal Ideation in College Students: Causal Factors and Intervention
text_snippet: Research Trends of Suicidal Ideation in College Students: Causal Factors and Intervention Suicidal ideation among university students has become a significant global mental health issue. Academic, social, and economic pressures increase students’ vulnerability to suicidal thoughts. Despite the growing number of studies, there is still no comprehensive bibliometric mapping that synthesizes research trends, risk factors, and interventions for the student population. This study aims to investigate the research trends related to suicidal ideation in students, identify contributing factors, and evaluate effective interventions. By employing a bibliometric approach and conducting a visual analysis of 382 documents from Scopus, the study uncovers common patterns and strategies that can be utilized to address this issue. The findings indicate that key risk factors include poor mental health, depression, and hopelessness. In contrast, social support, hope, and gratitude are emphasized as potential protective factors. Effective interventions identified in this study encompass enhancing social support, improving coping skills, ensuring access to mental health services, and implementing positive psychology-based therapies. title: The Moderating Role of Wisdom in Family Functioning and Anxiety amongst Indonesian Generation Z Adolescents
text_snippet: The Moderating Role of Wisdom in Family Functioning and Anxiety amongst Indonesian Generation Z Adolescents One contributing factor is poor family functioning, which refers to the inability of the family unit to meet the needs of family members through cohesive problem-solving, mutual care, and support in facing life's challenges. This study aims to examine the relationship between family functioning and anxiety among Generation Z (Gen Z) adolescents, as moderated by wisdom. To mitigate high levels of anxiety, the study positions wisdom as a moderator. It is proposed that wisdom can mitigate the negative impact of poor family functioning on anxiety by enabling emotional regulation, reflective thinking, and adaptive coping strategies. A quantitative methodology was employed using non-probability sampling, with 390 participants aged 17–27 in Indonesia. Data were collected through an online questionnaire consisting of four scales: Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) for anxiety; Family Adaptability and Cohesion Evaluation Scale II (FACES II) and Family Communication Scale (FCS) for family functioning; and Brief Self-Assessed Wisdom Scale (BSAWS) for wisdom. title: The Effectiveness of Bibliotherapy Using Flipbooks in Enhancing Resilience among Adolescents in Fatherless Situations
text_snippet: The Effectiveness of Bibliotherapy Using Flipbooks in Enhancing Resilience among Adolescents in Fatherless Situations The fatherless phenomenon experienced by adolescents has implications for low emotional resilience, thereby increasing vulnerability to psychosocial stress, anxiety, and reduced mental well-being. This study aims to examine the effectiveness of bibliotherapy using digital flipbook media in enhancing the emotional resilience of adolescents in fatherless situations. The research employed a quantitative approach with a one-group pretest-posttest pre-experimental design. The sample consisted of 20 seventh-grade junior high school students selected through purposive sampling. The instrument used was a resilience questionnaire comprising 60 valid and reliable statements (α = 0.975). Data were analyzed using N-Gain and Wilcoxon tests. The results indicated a significant increase in students’ resilience after receiving flipbook-based bibliotherapy intervention. N-Gain scores ranged from 0.37 to 0.92, categorized as moderate to high, while the Wilcoxon test yielded T1 = 0 and T2 = 1614, indicating a significant difference between pretest and posttest scores. title: The Hermeneutics of Values in the Novel A Portion of Chicken Noodles Before Dying as a Source of Existential Counseling Intervention
text_snippet: The Hermeneutics of Values in the Novel A Portion of Chicken Noodles Before Dying as a Source of Existential Counseling Intervention Many individuals experience confusion regarding the meaning and purpose of life due to the pressure of social comparison, making it difficult for them to fully understand themselves. This study aims to analyze the existential values in the novel Seporsi Mie Ayam Sebelum Mati as a source of existential counseling intervention. The study was conducted using Gadamer's hermeneutic approach and data analysis using the Miles and Huberman model, allowing for in-depth interpretation of the characters' experiences and the existential values contained therein. The results show that freedom, suffering, hope, openness, and responsibility are the main themes in the characters' journeys to find the meaning of life. Relevant to existential counseling interventions, it can strengthen counselors in helping clients become more aware of their life choices, accept themselves, find their direction in life, manage emotional wounds, and take ownership of their lives. These findings confirm that literary works can function as a reflective medium and help clients understand the meaning of life more deeply. title: Career Development Assessment Tools for Indonesian Adolescents: A Psychometric Study
text_snippet: Career Development Assessment Tools for Indonesian Adolescents: A Psychometric Study Indonesian adolescents face critical challenges in making career decisions, while limited access to culturally valid assessment tools further complicates their efforts to navigate this important developmental task. This study aimed to validate a career development assessment tool by 1) exploring its latent factor structure, 2) confirming the factorial model, and 3) evaluating its internal consistency reliability. Employing a quantitative cross-sectional survey design, a total of 743 adolescents completed an online 34-item instrument. Data were analyzed using exploratory factor analysis (EFA) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA). These results find EFA identified a stable three-factor structure comprising personal goals, self-efficacy beliefs, and outcome expectations, consistent with the Social Cognitive Career Theory framework. These dimensions demonstrated theoretical coherence and empirical support through strong item loadings and meaningful inter-factor correlations. title: SEHATI: Development of an Educational Board Game for Interactive Sexual Education of Individuals with Hearing Impairments
text_snippet: SEHATI: Development of an Educational Board Game for Interactive Sexual Education of Individuals with Hearing Impairments The lack of interactive and accessible learning media remains a major challenge in delivering sexual education to individuals with hearing impairments. This condition potentially leads to limited understanding of reproductive health and safe sexual behavior among this group. This study aimed to analyze and evaluate the effectiveness of developing the SEHATI educational board game as a learning medium to enhance sexual education understanding among individuals with hearing impairments. This research employed a research and development (R&D) approach using an instructional media development design. The research subjects consisted of two media experts, two subject-matter experts, and ten students with hearing impairments involved in a limited trial. Data were collected through observations, interviews, and feasibility questionnaires, using expert validation sheets and user response questionnaires as research instruments. Data were analyzed using quantitative and qualitative descriptive analysis to determine the feasibility of the developed media and students’ responses to the educational board game. title: Psychometric Properties of the General Self-efficacy Scale in Indonesian Senior High School Students: Invariance Across Gender
text_snippet: Psychometric Properties of the General Self-efficacy Scale in Indonesian Senior High School Students: Invariance Across Gender The measurement instruments assessing self-efficacy among Indonesian high school students have yet to establish cultural relevance and measurement equivalence across gender groups, raising the potential for biased gender comparisons. Without strong psychometric evidence, the interpretation of research findings and the design of educational interventions remain limited. This study aimed to adapt and comprehensively evaluate the psychometric properties of the Indonesian version of the General Self-Efficacy Scale (GSES) and to examine its measurement invariance across gender. Using a cross-sectional survey design, data were collected from 635 students and analyzed through Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) and multigroup procedures to assess configural, metric, scalar, and strict invariance. The results supported a three-factor, ten-item solution, with satisfactory model fit indices (CFI = 0.943; RMSEA = 0.066; SRMR = 0.043) and high internal consistency (Cronbach’s α = 0.85). Measurement invariance testing confirmed gender equivalence across all levels. title: A Pilot Study on the Effects of Mindfulness-Based Journaling on the Psychological Well-Being of Preschoolers' Parents
text_snippet: A Pilot Study on the Effects of Mindfulness-Based Journaling on the Psychological Well-Being of Preschoolers' Parents Preschoolers' parents often face psychological challenges that can affect their well-being and caregiving. Mindfulness-based journaling may offer a practical and accessible strategy to support psychological well-being. This pilot study used a mixed-methods design to evaluate the feasibility and preliminary effectiveness of a mindfulness-based journaling program for prechoolers’ parents in Indonesia. Twenty participants completed six days of guided journaling based on Ryff’s six dimensions of psychological well-being. Quantitative data were collected using the Indonesian-adapted version of the Ryff Psychological Well-Being Scale (RPWBS) and analyzed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test and normalized gain scores. Results showed statistically significant improvements across all dimensions, though normalized gain indicated low practical effectiveness A thematic analysis of participants’ journal entries was conducted using deductive and inductive approaches. Participants generally found the intervention helpful, with several expressing a willingness to continue journaling independently. title: The Social Media Paradox: A Correlation Analysis of Fear of Missing Out and Social Anxiety in Adolescent Social Media Users
text_snippet: The Social Media Paradox: A Correlation Analysis of Fear of Missing Out and Social Anxiety in Adolescent Social Media Users The development of social media has expanded the social interaction of adolescents, but also triggered the emergence of Fear of Missing out (FoMO) the fear of being left behind from the experiences of others or those around them. This phenomenon is thought to contribute to increased social anxiety. The purpose of this study was to analyze the empirical relationship between FoMO and social anxiety in adolescent social media users. The subjects of this study consisted of 84 students of Class XI were selected through saturated sampling technique. Data collection was conducted using the FOMO scale based on the theory of Pryblylski and the scale of social anxiety which has been tested for validity (r ≥ 0.30) and reliability (α >0.89). Data analysis using pearson product Moment correlation. The results showed no significant relationship (r = 0.012; p = 0.911) between FoMO and social anxiety. These findings indicate that FoMO does not directly affect social anxiety, but rather is moderated by internal factors such as self-regulation and social support. title: Development of a Psychological Well-Being Instrument in Secondary Schools
text_snippet: Development of a Psychological Well-Being Instrument in Secondary Schools Psychological well-being is a crucial psychological condition that every individual should possess, as a high level of psychological well-being contributes significantly to the overall course of a person’s life. The purpose of this study is to develop a psychological well-being instrument that can be used to identify an individual’s psychological well-being condition. This research employed a Research and Development (R&D) approach using the 4D design model. The respondents of this study consisted of 129 high school students. Data analysis for the instrument development utilized Aiken’s V, Pearson’s product-moment correlation, and Cronbach’s Alpha. The results of the study produced a valid psychological well-being instrument consisting of 48 items and a reliable coefficient with a Cronbach’s Alpha value of 0.876. The implication of this instrument development, in general, is that educators and educational practitioners can accurately identify students’ psychological well-being conditions through the administration of this instrument. title: Psychoeducational Intervention: An Effort to Prevent Early Marriage at Sebatik
text_snippet: Psychoeducational Intervention: An Effort to Prevent Early Marriage at Sebatik Child marriage constitutes a violation of child rights and a form of gender-based violence that significantly impacts human capital and restricts children's life opportunities. This phenomenon is highly alarming, where its prevalence is among the highest nationally, thus necessitating a focused intervention. The primary goal of this research is to develop a structured psychoeducation intervention design and evaluate its effectiveness by analyzing students' knowledge improvement concerning the definition, causes, impacts, and prevention efforts of child marriage. The study employed a quantitative experimental method with a One-group Pretest-Posttest design on students using purposive sampling. Data were collected via questionnaires and analyzed using the t-test. title: Reality Group Counseling to Reduce Phubbing Behavior in College Students
text_snippet: Reality Group Counseling to Reduce Phubbing Behavior in College Students The background of this study is the high prevalence of phubbing behavior, which has a negative impact on college students' social interactions. Through reality group counseling, external control behavior can be changed to internal control behavior, resulting in pleasure and enjoyment in life. This study aims to analyze the effectiveness of reality group counseling in reducing phubbing behavior among college students. A quantitative approach with a quasi-experiment using a pretest-posttest control group design was used. Data were collected using a phubbing behavior scale. The scale used in this study was the phubbing behavior scale for college students. This study involved a population of 37 students and a sample of 16 students. The sampling technique was done randomly. Data analysis was performed using an independent samples t-test, while the n-gain test was applied to assess the effectiveness of the intervention. Phubbing behavior was reduced through reality group counseling using the WDEP technique, which was conducted over 8 sessions, followed by a posttest using the phubbing behavior scale. title: Hope, Optimism, Academic Flow, and Academic Engagement of Students in Online Learning
text_snippet: Hope, Optimism, Academic Flow, and Academic Engagement of Students in Online Learning Online learning after the pandemic has brought new challenges, especially low student engagement due to distractions, decreased motivation, and increased academic workload. In addition, there is still limited research that simultaneously examines the role of positive psychological factors, namely hope, optimism, and flow experience, in comprehensively improving academic engagement. This study aims to analyze the relationship between hope, optimism, academic flow, and student academic engagement in online learning. The research design uses a correlational quantitative approach with multiple regression analysis. The participants consisted of 152 students. The instruments used included the Hope Scale, Optimism Scale, Academic Flow Scale, and Academic Engagement Scale. The results show that there is a significant simultaneous influence of expectations, optimism, and academic flow on academic engagement. Partially, these three variables also have a significant influence on academic engagement. title: Gamifying Career Guidance: A Quasi-Experimental Study Using the Career Snakes and Ladders Game
text_snippet: Gamifying Career Guidance: A Quasi-Experimental Study Using the Career Snakes and Ladders Game Career awareness among junior high school students remains low due to the lack of interactive and engaging guidance approaches. Conventional lecture-based career counseling often fails to spark student interest or encourage meaningful reflection about their future. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of the Career Snakes and Ladders Simulation Game as a group guidance medium to enhance career awareness. A quantitative experimental method with a quasi-experimental design was employed. The sample consisted of 20 eighth-grade students divided into experimental and control groups. The experimental group participated in a one-hour simulation game session, while the control group received traditional lecture-based guidance. Data were collected using a validated Career Awareness Questionnaire and analyzed using the Mann-Whitney U test. Results showed a significant improvement in the experimental group (p = 0.001) with a large effect size (Cohen’s d = 2.543). The game proved effective as a medium to increase students’ career awareness through movement-based, interactive, and engaging strategies. title: Scale of Teacher Support Related to Career and Impact Validation Assessment of its Effect on Career Decision Making Self-Efficacy
text_snippet: Scale of Teacher Support Related to Career and Impact Validation Assessment of its Effect on Career Decision Making Self-Efficacy Adolescents often rely on support from significant adult figures particularly parents and teachers to navigate their career development, yet research exploring the specific influence of teacher support on students’ career-related outcomes remains limited. This study aims to examine the factorial structure and measurement invariance of the Indonesian adaptation of the Teacher Support Scale (TSS). Using a quantitative survey design, the study involved 662 high school students who completed the Indonesian version of the TSS consisting of 21 items across four dimensions. Data were analyzed using multi-group confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) to assess configural, metric, scalar, and strict invariance across gender. The findings demonstrate that the Indonesian TSS exhibits strong internal reliability and retains its four-factor structure consistently for both male and female students. Furthermore, all invariance models met acceptable fit criteria, indicating that the scale functions equivalently across gender groups.
